name: Update Stage
description: Scene.update() traverses all primitives, tilesets, and data sources. Each object updates its state, computes transforms, and prepares render commands for the current frame.

name: Frustum Culling Stage
description: Performs view-frustum culling to determine which primitives and tiles are visible. Objects outside the camera frustum are excluded from rendering to reduce draw calls.

name: Command Build Stage
description: After update, each primitive produces DrawCommand objects. Commands are sorted into render queues (opaque, translucent, compute) and assigned RenderState, shader programs, and uniform maps.

name: Depth Pass
description: The depth pre-pass writes depth values for opaque geometry without color output. This populates the depth buffer used by subsequent passes for occlusion testing and depth comparisons.

name: Opaque Pass
description: Renders all opaque geometry sorted front-to-back. Uses the depth buffer from the depth pass to skip occluded fragments. This includes most primitives, terrain, and opaque 3D Tiles.

name: Translucent Pass
description: Renders translucent geometry sorted back-to-front. Depth writes are disabled to allow proper alpha blending. Includes translucent primitives, labels, billboards, and translucent 3D Tiles.

name: Classification Stage
description: Handles rendering of ClassificationPrimitive and GroundPrimitive with classificationType. Modifies the appearance of underlying 3D Tiles or terrain based on stencil buffer operations.

name: Picking Stage
description: Renders pickable objects to an offscreen framebuffer using unique pick colors. scene.pick() reads this framebuffer to determine which object is under the cursor.

name: 3D Tiles Traversal Stage
description: Traverses the 3D Tiles spatial tree (quadtree/octree/kd-tree) to determine which tiles to render based on screen-space error, visibility, and frustum culling. Manages tile loading, caching, and unloading.

name: Shader Compile Stage
description: Compiles and links GLSL shader programs. Includes vertex shaders, fragment shaders, and optional geometry shaders. Shader compilation may happen asynchronously and is cached by ShaderProgram.

name: Post-Process Stage
description: Applies post-processing effects after the main rendering passes. Includes bloom, ambient occlusion, FXAA anti-aliasing, and other screen-space effects applied via full-screen quad passes.

name: Primitive Release / Destroy Stage
description: Releases GPU resources when primitives are removed from the scene. Destroys WebGL buffers, textures, framebuffers, and shader programs to prevent memory leaks.
